attributes.description:
Background of the top bar where steps and progress live. A different tone from the body helps users see navigation vs. form content.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-background

Thickness of the border around the header. Use it to draw a clear line between the step rail and the content below.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-border-width

Border style for the header region: none, solid, dashed, or dotted.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-border-style

Color of the header outline. Transparent keeps the header open; a contrast color separates it from the wizard body.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-border-color

Corner rounding for the header. Align with the main wizard radius so the top and body feel like one component.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-border-radius

Padding inside the header around steps and labels. Increase on small screens so tap targets and text stay comfortable.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-padding

Shadow on the header only—adds depth under the progress area without lifting the whole wizard.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-box-shadow

Base header width; only meaningful in vertical orientation, which overrides this per appearance. Horizontal appearances never reference this var.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-heading-width

Base header height; only meaningful in vertical orientation, which overrides this per appearance. Horizontal appearances never reference this var.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-heading-height

How the header lays out: block stacks rows; flex lines up step navigation for horizontal scanning.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-display

How steps spread in the header: space-between balances few or many steps; flex-start, center, or flex-end pin the rail left, middle, or right for your layout.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-heading-justify-content

Space between the step marker, title, and helper text within each step. Clear spacing makes each step quicker to scan.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-gap

Background of the step navigation track—the band behind connectors and markers. Tints that rail separately from the rest of the header when you want a stronger progress strip.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-connector-background

Border color around each step row in the navigation. Subtle lines separate steps; transparent keeps the rail minimal.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-color

How strong the outline is around each step row. Thicker borders emphasize individual steps.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-width

Line style for step rows: solid, dashed, dotted, or none, plus other standard CSS border styles.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-style

Corner rounding for each step row. Pills or chips make tabs and stacked steps feel tappable and friendly.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-radius

Padding inside each step row so labels and markers aren't flush against the edges.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-padding

Shadow on individual step rows. Use sparingly to lift the active or hovered step without cluttering the rail.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-box-shadow

How the steps are aligned along the step strip: center, flex-start, flex-end, space-between. Prefix with safe (e.g. safe center) to keep the first step visible when the strip overflows.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-container-justify-content

Length of the connector lines along the step strip: the line's height in a vertical stepper, its width in a horizontal one. Use px, em, rem, or %.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-connector-height

Thickness of the connector lines, in both orientations. Tied to theme border width so the progress path matches other outlines. states.active / states.finished may override it; the value styles the line after that step.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-connector-width

Line style between markers: solid for a steady path, dashed or dotted for a lighter guide, none to hide connectors. states.active / states.finished may override it; the value styles the line after that step.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-connector-style

Color of the lines between steps. Should stay visible but quieter than active markers so progress is easy to follow. states.active / states.finished may override it; the value styles the line after that step.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-connector-color

Offset of the connector line: its top offset in a horizontal stepper, its left offset in a vertical one.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-connector-placement

Space between a step and its connector line (step.gap spaces the marker and the title inside a step).
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-connector-gap

Whether connector lines are drawn: block shows them, none hides them and frees their space.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-connector-display

Size of each step marker (number, dot, or icon). Larger targets are easier to see and align with touch-friendly layouts. Use px, em, or rem.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-size

Fill behind each step marker. A solid fill helps the current and completed steps stand out; transparent keeps the rail minimal.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-background

Ring thickness around each marker. Stronger rings make inactive steps easier to spot at a glance.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-border-width

Border style around markers: solid, dashed, dotted, or none.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-border-style

Outline color for step markers. Use contrast for clarity and to meet focus-state expectations.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-border-color

Shape of markers—fully rounded reads as chips or pills; smaller radius reads as squares with soft corners.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-border-radius

Shadow on markers. Light elevation can highlight the current step without overpowering labels.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-box-shadow

Space inside the marker around numbers or icons so glyphs don't touch the ring.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-padding

Color of each step's primary label in the navigation. Strong contrast helps users see where they are in the flow.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-title-color

Base title-label height; only meaningful for the classic appearance, which overrides this. Other appearances never reference this var.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-title-height

Base title-label background; only meaningful for the classic appearance, which overrides this. Other appearances never reference this var.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-title-background

Font for step labels next to markers. Use your theme's heading or label family so the wizard matches the rest of the app.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-title-font-family

Weight of step labels. Bolder text emphasizes the current step; lighter weight keeps long titles calmer.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-title-font-weight

Size of step labels. Larger type improves scan distance; smaller type fits more steps on one row.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-title-font-size

Line height when step labels wrap. Generous leading keeps multi-line titles readable in the rail.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-title-line-height

Letter spacing for step labels. Slight tracking can improve all-caps or short titles in narrow layouts.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-title-letter-spacing

Padding around each step label. Adds space between text and markers or connectors for clearer tap and read targets.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-title-padding

Color of supporting text under each step name. Keep it slightly softer than the title so hierarchy stays clear.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-description-color

Font for step helper text. Usually matches body or caption styles for a supportive, secondary feel.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-description-font-family

Weight of helper text under each step. Medium weights can improve skim reading without competing with titles.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-description-font-weight

Size of helper text. Smaller than titles so users notice the step name first, then optional context.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-description-font-size

Line height for helper text. Extra leading helps two-line hints stay readable under tight step columns.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-description-line-height

Letter spacing for helper text. Subtle tracking improves dense captions in the step rail.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-description-letter-spacing

Size of icons inside markers (checkmarks, arrows, etc.). Should feel balanced with step numbers and label text.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-icon-font-size

Color of icons inside markers (checkmarks, arrows, etc.). Should feel balanced with step numbers and label text.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-icon-color

Color of numbers inside step markers (for example 1, 2, 3). Should stay readable on both default and filled marker backgrounds.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-count-color

Typeface for numbers inside markers. Match the theme's numeric or label style for a consistent look.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-count-font-family

Weight of step numbers. Slightly bolder weights improve legibility at small sizes.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-count-font-weight

Size of numbers inside markers. Scale with indicator size so digits stay centered and easy to read.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-count-font-size

Line height for step numbers if they wrap. Keeps multi-digit or localized labels from clipping.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-count-line-height

Letter spacing for numbers in markers. Small tweaks help single digits look optically centered.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-count-letter-spacing

Base dot/marker size; only meaningful for the dottedstepper/dottedstepper-textinline appearances, which override this. Other appearances never reference this var.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-size

Layout mode for step items: inline-flex for a horizontal rail, flex for richer alignment, block for a vertical stack—match how users should scan the flow.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-display

Minimum width of each step. Lower it, or use fit-content, to let steps hug their labels.
CSS variable: --wm-wizardstepper-step-min-width

Space between the step marker, title, and helper text within each step. Clear spacing makes each step quicker to scan.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-gap

Padding inside each step row so labels and markers aren't flush against the edges.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-padding

Background of each step row in the navigation. Use fills or tints to show hover, focus, or grouping without changing the global track color.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-background

Border color around each step row in the navigation. Subtle lines separate steps; transparent keeps the rail minimal.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-color

How strong the outline is around each step row. Thicker borders emphasize individual steps.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-width

Line style for step rows: solid, dashed, dotted, or none, plus other standard CSS border styles.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-style

Corner rounding for each step row. Pills or chips make tabs and stacked steps feel tappable and friendly.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-radius

Shadow on individual step rows. Use sparingly to lift the active or hovered step without cluttering the rail.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-box-shadow
Placement of the line indicators in the wizard
Placement of the line indicators in the wizard

Placement of the line indicators in the wizard
Placement of the line indicators in the wizard

Background behind the tab-style step bar. A calm surface helps users treat steps like familiar tabs.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-heading-background

Layout mode for the tabstepper's heading row—typically flex so tabs distribute evenly or scroll as a row.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-heading-display

How tabs sit in the bar: space-around for even gaps, or space-between / flex-start / center / flex-end to anchor the strip for your content width.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-heading-justify-content

Padding around the tab row. Extra space keeps pill-shaped tabs from touching the wizard edge on small screens.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-heading-padding

Corner shape of the tab header area. Match step pills so the bar and tabs feel like one control.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-heading-border-radius

Border style for the tab header outline: none, solid, dashed, or dotted.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-heading-border-style

Border color for the tab header. Subtle lines separate the tab strip from content without looking heavy.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-heading-border-color

Thickness of the tab header border. Thicker edges can anchor the strip when the background is flat.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-heading-border-width

Fill for each tab-shaped step. Light surfaces read as clickable; match your tab pattern for instant familiarity.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-background

Outline color for each tab pill. Defines edges when steps sit on a similar background to the header.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-border-color

Border weight around each tab. Thicker strokes make inactive tabs easier to distinguish.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-border-width

Line style around tab pills: solid for crisp chips, dashed or dotted for softer separation.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-border-style

Roundness of each tab. Large radii give a pill look; tune so labels fit without clipping.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-border-radius

Space inside each tab around label and icon. Improves tap targets and keeps text off the pill edge.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-padding

Shadow on tab pills. A light lift can show selection; none keeps the bar flat and minimal.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-box-shadow

Corner rounding for each step row. Pills or chips make tabs and stacked steps feel tappable and friendly.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-radius

Border color around each step row in the navigation. Subtle lines separate steps; transparent keeps the rail minimal.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-color

How strong the outline is around each step row. Thicker borders emphasize individual steps.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-width

Line style for step rows: solid, dashed, dotted, or none, plus other standard CSS border styles.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-border-style

Shadow on individual step rows. Use sparingly to lift the active or hovered step without cluttering the rail.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-box-shadow

Padding inside each step row so labels and markers aren't flush against the edges.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-padding

Padding around tab labels. Balances text and icons inside each pill-shaped step.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-title-padding

Ring thickness around the marker inside a tab. Often set to 0 when the whole pill carries the state.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-indicator-border-width

Background behind the icon or number inside a tab. Transparent lets the pill color show through.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-step-indicator-background

Space for the marker inside each tab pill. fit-content hugs the icon or number; fixed sizes keep every tab visually even. Use px, em, or rem when not using fit-content.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-indicator-size
Placement of the line indicators in the wizard

Padding around labels on completed tabs. Keeps checkmarks and text aligned when the done state is quieter.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-finished-step-title-padding

Border color on completed tab labels. Use transparent to rely on icon or text alone for the done state.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-finished-step-title-border-color

Border weight on completed tab labels. Usually minimal so finished steps recede visually.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-finished-step-title-border-width

Border style for completed tab labels: typically none or solid for a subtle frame.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-finished-step-title-border-style

Corner rounding on completed tab labels. Match active tabs or flatten for a simpler done look.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-finished-step-title-border-radius

Shadow on completed tab labels. Usually none so finished steps don't compete with the active tab.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-finished-step-title-box-shadow

Marker background when a tab is complete. Transparent keeps focus on the check or success styling.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-finished-step-indicator-background

Background of the active step row in the navigation. Use fills or tints to show hover, focus, or grouping without changing the global track color.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-step-background

Padding around labels on completed tabs. Keeps checkmarks and text aligned when the done state is quieter.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-finished-step-title-padding

Label color on the selected tab. High contrast here tells users which step they are on.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-active-step-title-color

Outline color for the selected tab. Often matches the brand accent so the active step pops.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-active-step-title-border-color

Border weight on the selected tab. A thicker ring reinforces focus without replacing focus-visible styles.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-active-step-title-border-width

Border style for the selected tab—usually solid for a crisp selected chip.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-active-step-title-border-style

Corner rounding for the selected tab pill. Align with inactive tabs so only color and border change on selection.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-active-step-title-border-radius

Marker background on the selected tab. Transparent is common when the whole pill shows the active state.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-active-step-indicator-background

Icon tint on the selected tab. Match label color so icon and text read as one affordance.
CSS variable: --wm-wizard-tabstepper-states-active-step-icon-color
Placement of the line indicators in the wizard
